title: All-degree realization of coefficient shifted Tate constants
statement: Fix a finite field datum D and coefficient setting P [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with prime ell different from the characteristic, and let a_0:X_0 -> Spec D.k0 be separated of finite type. Use the native derived Weil category and its homology sheaves [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. Let c_0 compactify a_0 and S be a coefficient-normalized exceptional adjunction system [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Let Q be the common-stage geometric Frobenius pullback and Pairs its category of objects with an invertible structure QK -> K [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]. Define E_S as G_S(1) with structure the inverse-exchange right mate followed by G_S(theta_0); define T_d=H_d(1) with the actual root-line, tensor-unit and even-shift structure canonicalSourceTheta [def-pur-canonical-purity-source-transports, lem-pur-constant-purity-frobenius-square]. There exist functors C_n:Pairs -> WeilSheaf(D.k0,ell,X0) for all integers n such that (i) for every native exceptional right adjunction J, H^n(J(constant_point[0])) is isomorphic to C_n(E_S); (ii) for every natural d and integer n, C_n(T_d) is isomorphic to H^n((TateSheaf(d) tensor ConstantSheaf)[2d]) in the native Weil-sheaf category. The same comparison family is used in both clauses. No smoothness or purity is assumed, and no identification of E_S with T_d is asserted. These are comparisons of cohomology, not an equivalence between native derived Weil complexes and derived fixed pairs.

source.place: Final exceptional-adjunction paragraph, together with the canonical Tate-and-shift source of lem-pur-constant-purity-frobenius-square; retain arbitrary degree cohomology in the normalized comparison construction.

proof.text: Use the normalized exact common-stage realization, the section-module equivalence and equivariant algebraic-closure transport. Their Frobenius comparisons turn a coefficient Frobenius pair into a Frobenius pair in the ordinary derived category. Apply degree n cohomology and the exact-pullback cohomology comparison. The cohomology is bounded constructible, so the resulting pair is a native Weil sheaf. On arrows use cohomology of the same realization; the comparison naturality proves the intertwining condition and the functor laws. This constructs C_n for every integer n, without a derived fixed-pair equivalence.

source.place: Final exceptional-adjunction paragraph, combined with exact cohomology and the canonical constant/Tate source of the smooth dualizing specialization.

proof.text: At any native exceptional adjunction J, use the counit-normalized exceptional-forgetting comparison at the constant object on the arithmetic point, and its scalar-unit normalization. Transport the native counit equivariance through the normalized compact-support comparison, then transpose through the ordinary adjunction. Uniqueness under its Hom equivalence identifies the action with the inverse-exchange right mate followed by G(theta_0), as computed by the scalar Frobenius counit theorem. Exact cohomology of this comparison is the first family of endpoint isomorphisms.

source.place: Final exceptional-adjunction paragraph, combined with exact cohomology and the canonical constant/Tate source of the smooth dualizing specialization.

proof.text: For every natural d and integer n, realize the canonical purity-source pair H_d(1) using the same functors from step 1. Pullback-unit normalization identifies the constant factor. Tensor and root-line realization identifies its d-th Tate line, including cyclotomic Frobenius, with the native Tate sheaf tensor the native constant sheaf. The shift comparison carries the shift by 2d to the same native derived shift. Apply cohomology in degree n to obtain the second family, without specializing to n=-2d. The root, tensor, unit and shift comparisons are exactly those used in canonicalSourceTheta, so the comparison intertwines Frobenius. No smoothness or exceptional purity is used. At d=0 the root line and shift are units; on the empty scheme the statement is the unique comparison of zero sheaves.

source.place: Structure-morphism and constant-unit specialization; take cohomology of the coefficient purity isomorphism with its canonical Frobenius square.

proof_origin.place: All-degree version of the normalized coefficient cohomology construction; the source provides equivariance and exceptional adjunction, and the canonical root/tensor/shift normalizations provide the Tate endpoint.

theorem coefficient_shifted_tate_comparison :
    ∃ C : ℤ → (Pairs P X₀ ⥤ WeilSheaf P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l X₀.left),
      (∀ (J : WeilComplex P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l (Spec (.of P.field.k₀)) ⥤
          WeilComplex P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l X₀.left)
        (adj : WeilComplex.derivedLowerShriek P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l X₀.hom ⊣ J)
        (n : ℤ),
        Nonempty ((WeilComplex.homologySheaf n).obj
            (J.obj (WeilSheaf.toComplex.obj
              (WeilSheaf.adicConstant P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l
                (Spec (.of P.field.k₀))))) ≅
          (C n).obj (exceptionalConstant P X₀ c₀ S))) ∧
      (∀ (d : ℕ) (n : ℤ), Nonempty ((C n).obj (twistedConstant P X₀ d) ≅
        (WeilComplex.homologySheaf n).obj
          ((WeilSheaf.toComplex.obj
            ((WeilSheaf.tateTwistSheaf P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l X₀.left d).tensorObj
              (WeilSheaf.adicConstant P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l X₀.left)
              (WeilSheaf.isLisse_tateTwistSheaf P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l X₀.left d)))⟦
                2 * (d : ℤ)⟧)))
